gap: No result ChatGPT got states that US digital radio is HD Radio (IBOC), which the FCC approved on 11 October 2002, so a DAB/DAB+ radio like the JBL Tuner 2 it was shown works only as an FM radio in the US.
standout_why: I opened itechguides.com 'Best Bluetooth Speakers with FM Radio: 3 Top Picks for 2026' and rottenwifi.com 'Best Bluetooth Speakers With FM Radio in 2026'. Neither page mentions DAB, HD Radio or which digital radio standard the US uses. They only discuss FM, AM, shortwave and weather-band reception, plus advice on extending the telescopic antenna. ChatGPT's own results include a DAB product page (jbl.com Tuner 2, result 13) and a DAB buying guide (techradar.com 'best DAB radio', result 10), but nothing tells a US shopper that DAB isn't the US system. I didn't open the other rival pages (geekchamp, sekin, powersof10, gagadget, mobilestalk), so I can't rule out that one of them covers it.
decides: For a US shopper it rules out paying extra for DAB/DAB+ (JBL Tuner 2, TechRadar's DAB list), because the FCC chose HD Radio as the US digital system and DAB adds nothing there. The decision comes down to FM (or AM/FM) reception on the picks ChatGPT showed (Avantree, iHome, Tivoli). A second, smaller check: the Avantree BoomByte has a 'Campus Band' setting (76–90 MHz). If it is selected, the radio searches only 76–90 MHz and skips most of the 87–108 MHz band that US stations use, until you switch it to 'Common Band'.

findings.label: US digital radio standard chosen by the FCC
findings.value: HD Radio IBOC, approved 11 October 2002 as the US digital radio delivery method (not DAB)
findings.note: Page quote: "iBiquity's HD Radio™ IBOC technology was approved as the delivery method for digital radio broadcasting in the U.S." This follows the NRSC's 2001–2002 evaluation. The page is run by HD Radio itself, not the FCC.

findings.label: Radio bands
findings.value: FM, DAB and DAB+ (no HD Radio listed)
findings.source_title: JBL Tuner 2 | Portable DAB/DAB+/FM radio with Bluetooth
findings.note: The page is JBL's Myanmar storefront and links an EU/UK Declaration of Conformity. It gives no frequency ranges and doesn't say which regions the radio is meant for.

findings.label: FM band setting that limits tuning
findings.value: 'Campus Band' searches 76–90 MHz only; 'Common Band' searches 87–108 MHz
findings.source_title: FM Range Limited to 76–90 MHz – Avantree Support
findings.note: Quote: "If your Boombyte only searches between 76–90 MHz, it is likely set to Campus Band." Fix: in FM mode press ⚙️/OK, press SEEK < or SEEK > until Common Band appears, then press ⚙️/OK. The Boombyte Menu Overview page (https://support.avantree.com/hc/en-us/articles/47271864756249-Boombyte-Menu-Overview) describes Campus Band as using 'approximately 76–90 MHz'.

findings.label: FM antenna guidance in maker support
findings.value: Covers both kinds: pull-up antenna ('Extend the antenna all the way') and power-cord antenna ('Fully extend the power cord… Do not leave the cord rolled or bundled')
findings.source_title: Improve Reception & Reduce Static – Avantree Support
findings.note: The article is filed under 'Boombyte / BTSP-870' but its text doesn't say which antenna type the BoomByte has.
